judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'sudden and accidental' pollution exception is one of the most heavily litigated phrases in general liability insurance, and the text is further garbled by interleaved insuring-agreement lines.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Total Pollution Exclusion (c189–c192) expressly replaces this exclusion while the Pollution Liability Endorsement (c176–c182) grants claims-made pollution cover, so three pollution texts operate together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The war exclusion is intelligible but the reproduced text runs together with insuring-agreement and exclusion (a) fragments, and 'to any act or condition incident to any of the foregoing' is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A parallel war exclusion appears in the medical payments part (c145)(4), consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The liquor-liability and contractual-liability exclusions are interleaved in this text so that clause boundaries are lost, and 'except an incidental contract' is a general-versus-specific point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Host Liquor Law Liability Coverage (c152) restores cover excluded by (h), and the Broad Form widens 'incidental contract', so exclusion (a)'s reach depends on those texts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reproduced exclusion is a fragment merged with parts of exclusion (k) and is not a complete sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion (k) is separately replaced by the Broad Form Property Damage coverage (c156), so the printed text is partly superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The elevator and alienated-premises exclusions are run together and the operative words ('arising out of the use of an elevator') are partly lost in the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Broad Form property damage provisions (c156) create elevator carve-outs, which must be read against this exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A structured loss-of-use exclusion with an express 'sudden and accidental' exception; conventional business-risk language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with exclusions (n)-(p) and the Broad Form Property Damage rewrite (c156), which replaces (k) and (o) but not (m).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short products self-damage exclusion; specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with (o) and (p) and unaffected by the Broad Form rewrite except as stated there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard 'your work' exclusion; concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly replaced by the Broad Form Property Damage Liability Coverage (c156)(A), so the printed text no longer stands alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A sistership/recall exclusion with the familiar 'known or suspected defect or deficiency' test; standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision modifies it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion depends on classification code symbols 'x', 'c' and 'u', and the reproduced symbols are corrupted and the sentence truncated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The CGL schedule of hazards (c119 context) does not clearly show those symbols, so whether the exclusion bites cannot be determined from the policy as reproduced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated Persons Insured list with detailed provisos; each class is scope-limited.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Form 009-110 WI (c061–c062) says the CGL persons insured provisions 'are changed to read as follows', so this printed list is displaced while remaining in the policy alongside c161's additions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed limits structure with separate occurrence and aggregate rules and a 'continuous or repeated exposure' deeming clause; long but internally specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The GL 99 17 endorsement (c164–c167) expressly amends the same 'Limits of Liability' provisions to a combined single limit, so this text is superseded while remaining printed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence tying coverage to the defined policy territory; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limited Worldwide Liability Coverage (c160) amends the territory definition, an express and consistent expansion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The schedule leaves the personal injury aggregate blank and states it 'shall be the per occurrence bodily injury liability limit unless otherwise indicated', a default that requires cross-reading and produces no stated figure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The declarations show a $1,000,000 CGL occurrence limit while the GL 99 17 schedule (c164) shows $4,000,000 each occurrence and $1,000,000 aggregate, so the default in this schedule cannot be applied without resolving that discrepancy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reproduced text merges the contractual-liability exclusions with the (C) and (D) paragraphs so the numbering and boundaries are unintelligible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion (5) of this same paragraph is separately amended by GL 99 19 (c171), which supersedes part of the text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It disapplies exclusions identified only as '(b), (c)(2), (d) and (e)' and the reproduced letters are corrupted to '{0}, (c}(2), (a) and {e}', so which exclusions are disapplied is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The referenced exclusions live in the CGL coverage part (c123, c124), some of which are themselves replaced elsewhere, so the cross-reference chain is fragile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The company shall be entitled to exercise all of the insured's rights in the choice of arbitrators and in the conduct of any arbitration proceeding' is a strong, one-sided condition, and the reproduced text is scrambled with the exclusion above it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Suit' is elsewhere defined to include arbitration (c047), so how far the company's control extends across coverages is a question spanning provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional personal/advertising injury grant; the paragraph letters (A)(B)(C) are stranded at the top of the text but the grant reads coherently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its limit refers to an 'aggregate' stated in the endorsement, which is blank in the schedule (c134), so the grant's ceiling depends on another provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated exclusion list with a visible numbering error (two items numbered (3)) and the well-worn 'knowledge of the falsity' test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 3 (c067) amends the related definition to add 'Humiliation', which interacts with these offence-based exclusions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-aggregate limit clause; clear in structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It points to a figure 'stated in this endorsement as aggregate' which the schedule leaves blank subject to a default (c134), so the actual limit must be derived from the declarations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An offence-based definition listing libel, slander, piracy, unfair competition and infringement; 'unfair competition' is broad but the list is closed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the definition Endorsement 3 (c067) purports to amend by adding 'Humiliation', though (D)1 is in the personal injury list, not this one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing 'except' clause is ungrammatical ('except publications ... shall not be deemed personal injury'), which inverts the intended sense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 3 (c067) adds 'Humiliation' to item (D)1, which in this list is false arrest/detention/imprisonment — a mismatch between the amendment and the text amended.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant is materially garbled — the condition limbs ('a condition in the insured premises' / 'operations') are missing words — so the trigger cannot be read as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its exclusion (D) is deleted by Endorsement 8 (c088), which greatly expands medical payments for a hospital and must be reconciled with the HPL part's exclusivity clause (c050).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated auto/mobile equipment/watercraft exclusion; the sub-numbering is duplicated ('(2)' appears twice) but the substance is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the parallel CGL exclusions (b), (c) and (e); no competing text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Enumerated exclusions with the usual liquor-liability structure; specific rather than open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Host Liquor Law Liability Coverage (c152) restores liquor cover only for exclusion (h) of the CGL part, leaving this medical-payments exclusion in force — a distinction that must be drawn from the two texts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of excluded persons; the categories (tenants, employees, participants in athletic activity) are concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with the deletion of exclusion (D) (c088), the surviving exclusions define how far medical payments reach hospital patients, which is a document-wide question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence excluding medical expense for services by the named insured or its employees; unambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 8 (c088) declares 'Exclusion (D) of Section II - Premises Medical payments Coverage' null and void; if that reaches this clause it is deleted, and if the section reference is fatal it survives — a direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A per-person/per-accident limits structure keyed to a $1,000 default; arithmetically definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It caps aggregate medical payments by reference to the bodily injury 'each occurrence' limit in the policy, which the declarations and the GL 99 17 schedule (c164) state differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All premises owned by or rented to the named insured with respect to which the named insured is afforded coverage' is circular in part but workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The CGL schedule of locations is amended repeatedly (c207, c209, c215, c217), so which premises are 'insured premises' changes through the term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated medical-expense definition ending in a specific list; closed and concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No competing definition of medical expense appears elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Proof-of-claim and examination duties with 'as soon as practicable' and 'as often as the company may reasonably require'; standard reasonableness language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the insured's duties conditions (c023, c048) without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Functions incidental to the named insured's business' is a soft boundary, but the proviso about not being in the liquor business is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restores cover excluded by CGL exclusion (h) (c123) but not by the medical-payments exclusion (c145)(3), a difference that must be read across the endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All of the exclusions of the policy ... are deleted and replaced' is an extraordinarily sweeping formula whose reach across a policy with dozens of endorsement-added exclusions is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot easily be reconciled with later-added exclusions such as the Total Pollution Exclusion (c189) and the nuclear exclusion (c198), which the clause purports to preserve only in part.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stated $50,000 per-occurrence limit; the figure is rendered '550,000' in the text, a visible typographical error affecting the number.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The schedule (c134) leaves the fire legal figure blank subject to the same $50,000 default, so the two are consistent once the typo is read through.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An excess-insurance clause listing specific property covers followed by 'such as, but not limited to', a general-after-specific formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly amends the Other Insurance condition (c027), which declares the policy primary, so the two must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The replacement exclusions are long and technical, and the reproduced text is broken by page headers so that paragraph boundaries are lost.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces CGL exclusions (k) and (o) (c128 and the (k) text within c124), which remain printed elsewhere in the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same excess-insurance formula as the fire legal clause; 'such as, but not limited to' is a general catch-all after specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It too amends the Other Insurance condition (c027) 'accordingly', without saying how it interacts with c155's parallel amendment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Incidental' medical malpractice is nowhere defined, and exclusion (2) removes 'any insured engaged in the business or occupation of providing any of the services described' — for a hospital that arguably swallows the coverage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The HPL part states that except as stated there the policy does not apply to injury caused by any medical incident (c050), which squarely conflicts with this CGL grant of medical malpractice cover.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A watercraft carve-back with a length limit and a no-contribution sentence; the figures are precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its no-contribution sentence sits alongside the Other Insurance condition (c027) and the excess clauses (c155, c157), adding a fourth other-insurance rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Permanently domiciled' and the numbering of the added paragraph as '4.' when the base definition has three limbs are minor mechanical wrinkles.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It amends the policy territory definition (c016) while the HPL part has its own territory clause amended twice (c045, c172, c205), so territory is governed by four texts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds spouses and employees as insureds with detailed carve-outs; specific and structured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds insureds under 'Persons Insured', a provision already rewritten by Form 009-110 WI (c062), which itself already includes employees — so the two additions overlap with different exclusions attached.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable force for the purpose of protecting persons or property' is an evaluative standard, and 'solely' does heavy work in a hospital-restraint context.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It rewrites the 'occurrence' definition (c015), which excludes expected or intended injury, so the two definitions must be read together to determine the trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Maintains ownership or majority interest' and the ninety-day sunset are specific, though the provision's own proviso structure is convoluted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Additional Named Insureds form (c092) expressly says 'no automatic coverage for entities newly acquired by any of them is extended hereby', which contradicts this automatic ninety-day grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The schedule states $4,000,000 each occurrence against a $1,000,000 aggregate — an aggregate smaller than the per-occurrence limit, which is internally incoherent as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The declarations state $1,000,000 each occurrence and $1,000,000 aggregate for CGL bodily injury, so the endorsement schedule and the declarations do not match.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A combined single-limit rule with a financial-responsibility proviso; long but internally definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the endorsement schedule figures (c164), which conflict with the declarations, and it replaces the printed CGL limits (c132).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The aggregate provision is reproduced with a stray fragment ('to Bodily Injury Liability and Property Damage Liability are amended to read as') dropped into the middle of subparagraph (1), breaking the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It rewrites the aggregate structure of c132 and applies annually, which interacts with the Three Year Policy condition (c033) and the declared one-year term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single deeming sentence on continuous or repeated exposure; concise and standard, but the number-of-occurrences question it answers is perennially litigated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the closing sentence of c132 and parallels the medical-incident aggregation rule (c046), which uses a different, per-person test.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Loading or unloading' is defined with an express mechanical-device carve-out; the phrase is nevertheless a classic site of dispute over where handling begins and ends.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: HPL exclusion (d) as amended (c188) deems loading and unloading of patients to be health care services, and c071 adds air ambulances, so this property-based definition sits awkwardly with the patient-based rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear prejudgment-interest addition with a definite cut-off tied to an offer of limits.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds to the Supplementary Payments provision (c002), which also addresses post-judgment interest, and is limited by the nuclear endorsement (c199) for first-aid expenses only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The replacement exclusion's lettering is corrupted ('a)', 'Git}', 'Cay') and the phrase 'in any other capacity' greatly widens the employer's-liability bar in a contested way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says it replaces 'the exclusion relating to bodily injury to any employee of the insured' without identifying the coverage part, so whether it displaces HPL exclusion (a) (c039) as well as the CGL exclusion is unresolved.
